You're on the right lines with Bluetooth Low Energy. However this is quite a big project to start with. Firstly know that Bluetooth devices such as the one you posted offer "services" that vary based on your application. A typical phone only offers some services, namely audio streaming, headset (microphone and earpiece), peripherals (keyboard)...etc whereas computers which are more sophisticated offer more. These are complicated to get your head round but Bluetooth version 4.0 which is what BLE comes under only has two: GAP and GATT. GAP deals with the "discovery" process and GATT the "what happens after the user has connected" process. These two make BLE easier to work with, read more about it here: https://learn.adafruit.com/introduction-to-bluetooth-low-energy/introduction.

Once you understand the basics of how bluetooth works and what services are etc you'll find that sending data from an iphone to a module is easy. See example apps such as https://itunes.apple.com/gb/app/lightblue-bluetooth-low-energy/id557428110?mt=8 and the developer documents: https://developer.apple.com/library/ios/documentation/NetworkingInternetWeb/Conceptual/CoreBluetooth_concepts/AboutCoreBluetooth/Introduction.html

However the hard part is the electronic bluetooth module. You need a microcontroller to be connected to this. Some bluetooth modules are intelligent and come with built in processors but I recommend you don't buy one of these. They are more complicated and will require expensive hardware to program them. The instructables link you posted uses one of these as does the module on fasttech that you posted. Don't get me wrong they're excellent devices but for a beginner you'll want something simpler.

Simpler devices require an external microcontroller to control the bluetooth functionality. I recommend this for you. See this tutorial: https://learn.adafruit.com/getting-started-with-the-nrf8001-bluefruit-le-breakout/introduction

You'll notice this uses a microcontroller called an Arduino. This is perfect for beginners and there are literally hundreds of tutorials out there for starting Arduino programming: http://www.ladyada.net/learn/arduino/

You mentioned in your post that you need to connect your bluetooth module, motor and battery together. This is what the Arduino does. Start simple. Get the Arduino to flash a light on and off. Then a motor. Then follow the bluetooth tutorial above to get your iphone to turn an LED on and off and finally a motor on and off.

You've chosen a big project to start with but if you have the patience there's no reason you can't do it. The Arduino tutorial I posted has everything you need to get started. After you've mastered that getting a bluetooth module like the one in the tutorial I posted will be easy.

Yeah that's exactly the sort of thing you need. The 2nd tutorial you posted is a based around "wearable electronics". Those are designed to be sewn into clothes and use conductive thread rather than standard wires.

But yeah the trinket and the SPI friend are both perfect. Easy to use and exactly what you need. UART and SPI are both types of communication that any micro controller can deal with. SPI is faster than UART but UART is easier to understand and use. Since you'll be sending simple commands to let the trinket know a notification has occurred and thus the motor needs turning on for whatever length of time, you don't need a fast complicated protocol such as SPI. But in future projects (if you decide) then you'll find SPI to be very useful
